The precylinder object obtained by switching the two inclusions.
The gluing of two precylinders.
the map from the coproduct of two copies of `A` to `P.I`, when `P` is a cylinder object for `A`. `P` shall be a *good* cylinder object when this morphism is a cofibration.
The precylinder in a full subcategory of `C` induced by a precylinder in the category `C`.
The image of a precylinder by a functor.

files.t: The left derivability structure attached to a model category
files.s: We show that the inclusion of the full subcategory of cofibrant objects in a model category is a left derivability structure. This is the dual to Corollaire 10.10 in [the paper by Kahn and Maltsiniotis][KahnMaltsiniotis2008].

files.t: The right derivability structure attached to a model category
files.s: We show that the inclusion of the full subcategory of fibrant objects in a model category is a right derivability structure. This is Corollaire 10.10 in [the paper by Kahn and Maltsiniotis][KahnMaltsiniotis2008].

files.t: The homotopy category of fibrant objects
files.s: Let `C` be a model category. By using the left homotopy relation, we introduce the homotopy category `FibrantObject.HoCat C` of fibrant objects in `C`, and we define a fibrant resolution functor `FibrantObject.HoCat.resolution : C ⥤ FibrantObject.HoCat C`.

h.d: The left homotopy relation on the category of fibrant objects.
The homotopy category of fibrant objects.
The quotient functor from the category of fibrant objects to its homotopy category.
The functor `FibrantObject C ⥤ HoCat C`, considered as a localizer morphism.
Given `X : C`, this is a fibrant object `X'` equipped with a trivial cofibration `X ⟶ X'` (see `HoCat.iResolutionObj`).
This is a trivial cofibration `X ⟶ resolutionObj X` where `resolutionObj X` is a choice of a fibrant resolution of `X`.

files.t: The fundamental lemma of homotopical algebra
files.s: Let `C` be a model category. Let `L : C ⥤ H` be a localization functor with respect to weak equivalences in `C`. We obtain the fundamental lemma of homotopical algebra: if `X` is cofibrant and `Y` fibrant, the map `(X ⟶ Y) → (L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y)` identifies `L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y` to the quotient of `X ⟶ Y` by the homotopy relation (in this case, the left and right homotopy…

h.d: The map `LeftHomotopyClass X Y → (L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y)` when `L` is a localization functor with respect to `weakEquivalences C`.
The map `RightHomotopyClass X Y → (L.obj X ⟶ L.obj Y)` when `L` is a localization functor with respect to `weakEquivalences C`.

files.t: Homotopies in model categories
files.s: In this file, we relate left and right homotopies between morphisms `X ⟶ Y` in model categories. In particular, if `X` is cofibrant and `Y` is fibrant, these notions coincide (for arbitrary choices of good cylinders or good path objects).

h.d: When two morphisms `X ⟶ Y` with `X` cofibrant are related by a left homotopy, this is a choice of a right homotopy relative to any good path object for `Y`.
When two morphisms `X ⟶ Y` with `Y` fibrant are related by a right homotopy, this is a choice of a left homotopy relative to any good cylinder object for `X`.
When two morphisms `X ⟶ Y` with `X` cofibrant and `Y` fibrant are related by a left homotopy, this is a choice of a left homotopy relative to any good cylinder object for `X`.
When two morphisms `X ⟶ Y` with `X` cofibrant and `Y` fibrant are related by a right homotopy, this is a choice of a right homotopy relative to any good path object for `Y`.
Left homotopy classes of maps `X ⟶ Y` identify to right homotopy classes when `X` is cofibrant and `Y` is fibrant.

files.t: Consequences of model category axioms
files.s: In this file, we deduce basic properties of fibrations, cofibrations, and weak equivalences from the axioms of model categories.

files.t: Fibrant and cofibrant objects in a model category
files.s: Once a category `C` has been endowed with a `CategoryWithCofibrations C` instance, it is possible to define the property `IsCofibrant X` for any `X : C` as an abbreviation for `Cofibration (initial.to X : ⊥_ C ⟶ X)`. (Fibrant objects are defined similarly.)

h.d: An object `X` is cofibrant if `⊥_ C ⟶ X` is a cofibration.
An object `X` is fibrant if `X ⟶ ⊤_ C` is a fibration.

files.t: A trick by Joyal
files.s: In order to construct a model category, we may sometimes have basically proven all the axioms with the exception of the left lifting property of cofibrations with respect to trivial fibrations. A trick by Joyal allows to obtain this lifting property under suitable assumptions, namely that cofibrations are stable under composition and cobase change.

h.d: Joyal's trick (dual): that trivial cofibrations have the left lifting property with respect to fibrations follows from the left lifting property of cofibrations with respect to trivial fibrations and a few other…

Given a precylinder `P` for `X`, two maps `f` and `g` in `X ⟶ Y` are homotopic relative to `P` when there is a morphism `h : P.I ⟶ Y` such that `P.i₀ ≫ h = f` and `P.i₁ ≫ h = g`.

files.t: Path objects
files.s: We introduce a notion of path object for an object `A : C` in a model category. It consists of an object `P`, a weak equivalence `ι : A ⟶ P` equipped with two retractions `p₀` and `p₁`. This notion shall be important in the definition of "right homotopies" in model categories.

h.d: A pre-path object for `A : C` is the data of a morphism `ι : A ⟶ P` equipped with two retractions.
The pre-path object obtained by switching the two projections.
The gluing of two pre-path objects.
The map from `P.P` to the product of two copies of `A`, when `P` is a pre-path object for `A`. `P` shall be a *good* path object when this morphism is a fibration.
The pre-path object in a full subcategory of `C` induced by a pre-path object in the category `C`.
The image of a pre-path object by a functor.

files.s: We introduce the types `PrepathObject.RightHomotopy` and `PathObject.RightHomotopy` of homotopies between morphisms `X ⟶ Y` relative to a (pre)path object of `Y`. Given two morphisms `f` and `g`, we introduce the relation `RightHomotopyRel f g` asserting the existence of a path object `P` and a right homotopy `P.RightHomotopy f g`, and we define the quotient type…

`f : X ⟶ Y` is right homotopic to itself relative to any pre-path object.

If `f₀` is homotopic to `f₁` relative to a pre-path object `P`, and `f₁` is homotopic to `f₂` relative to `P'`, then `f₀` is homotopic to `f₂` relative to `P.trans P'`.
Right homotopies are compatible with precomposition.

files.t: Transport a model category via an equivalence
files.s: Given an equivalence of categories `e : C ≌ D`, we transport a model category structure on `D` in order to obtain a model category structure on `C`. files.t: Moore complex
files.s: We construct the normalized Moore complex, as a functor `SimplicialObject C ⥤ ChainComplex C ℕ`, for any abelian category `C`.

h.d: The normalized Moore complex in degree `n`, as a subobject of `X n`.
The differentials in the normalized Moore complex.
The normalized Moore complex functor, on objects.
The normalized Moore complex functor, on morphisms.
The (normalized) Moore complex of a simplicial object `X` in an abelian category `C`. The `n`-th object is the intersection of the kernels of `X.δ i : X.obj n ⟶ X.obj (n-1)`, for `i = 1, ..., n`.

files.t: Quasicategories
files.s: In this file we define quasicategories, a common model of infinity categories. We show that every Kan complex is a quasicategory.

h.d: A simplicial set `S` is a *quasicategory* if it satisfies the following horn-filling condition: for every `n : ℕ` and `0 < i < n`, every map of simplicial sets `σ₀ : Λ[n, i] → S` can be extended to a map `σ : Δ[n] → S`.

files.t: Composition of edges in quasicategories
files.s: In this file, we define the notions of left and right homotopies on edges of simplicial sets, and we show that if `X` is a quasicategory, then edges can be composed (see `SSet.Edge.comp` and `SSet.Edge.compStruct`) and that this composition satisfies some form of associativity. The results are deduced from similar results for `2`-truncated quasicategories.

h.d: A left homotopy between two edges `e` and `e'` is a `CompStruct e (id _) e'`.
A right homotopy between two edges `e` and `e'` is a `CompStruct (id _) e e'`.
The composition of two edges in a quasicategory.
If `e₀₁ : Edge x₀ x₁` and `e₁₂ : Edge x₁ x₂` are edges in a quasicategory, this is a structure exhibiting the fact that `e₀₁.comp e₁₂` is a composition of `e₀₁` and `e₁₂`.
The associativity of the composition of edges in a quasicategory.

files.t: Inner fibrations
files.s: Inner fibrations of simplicial sets are the morphisms in `SSet` which have the right lifting property with respect to all inner horn inclusions.

h.d: The family of morphisms in `SSet` which consists of inner horn inclusions `Λ[n, i].ι : Λ[n, i] ⟶ Δ[n]` (for `0 < i < n`).
The inner fibrations are the morphisms which have the right lifting property with respect to inner horn inclusions.
A morphism `q` satisfies `[InnerFibration q]` if it belongs to `innerFibrations`.

files.t: The nerve of a category is a quasicategory
files.s: In `AlgebraicTopology.Quasicategory.StrictSegal`, we show that any strict Segal simplicial set is a quasicategory. In `AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StrictSegal`, we show that the nerve of a category satisfies the strict Segal condition.

files.t: The strict bicategory of quasicategories
files.s: In this file we define a strict bicategory `QCat.strictBicategory` whose objects are quasicategories.

h.d: `QCat` is the category of quasi-categories defined as the full subcategory of the category `SSet` of simplicial sets.
The underlying category of the `Cat`-enriched ordinary category of quasicategories is equivalent to `QCat`.

files.t: Strict Segal simplicial sets are quasicategories
files.s: In `AlgebraicTopology.SimplicialSet.StrictSegal`, we define the strict Segal condition on a simplicial set `X`. We say that `X` is strict Segal if its simplices are uniquely determined by their spine.

h.d: Any `StrictSegal` simplicial set is a `Quasicategory`.

files.t: 2-truncated quasicategories and homotopy relations
files.s: We define 2-truncated quasicategories `Quasicategory₂` by three horn-filling properties, and the left and right homotopy relations `HomotopicL` and `HomotopicR` on the edges in a 2-truncated simplicial set.

h.d: Given edges `f`, `g` and `h` of a `2`-truncated quasicategory, there exists a structure `CompStruct f g h` iff `homMk f ≫ homMk g = homMk h` holds in the homotopy category.
A `CompStruct f g h` is a witness for the fact that the morphisms represented by `f` and `g` compose to the morphism represented by `h`.
Right homotopic edges represent the same morphism in the homotopy category.
Left homotopic edges represent the same morphism in the homotopy category.
The trivial (degenerate) edge at a vertex `x` is a representative for the identity morphism `x ⟶ x`.
Every morphism in the homotopy category `HomotopyCategory₂ X` is the equivalence class of an edge of `A`.

files.t: The truncation of a quasicategory
files.s: In this file, we show that if `X : SSet` is a quasicategory, then `((truncation 2).obj X)` satisfies the property `SSet.Truncated.Quasicategory₂`.

files.t: Reedy categories
files.s: In this file, we introduce the definition of a Reedy structure on a category `C` equipped with two classes of morphisms `W₁` and `W₂` (these are sometimes denoted `C₋` and `C₊` in the literature).

h.d: A Reedy structure on a category `C` equipped with two multiplicative classes of morphisms `W₁` and `W₂` consists of the data of a degree map for objects `deg : C → α`, where `α` is a well ordered type.
The opposite of a Reedy structure.
The Reedy factorization of a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` as a morphism in `W₁` followed by a morphism in `W₂`.
